thread.title_full: Exclusive first look at Jamestown's Beech restaurant under new chef - NewsBreak

author: Gail Ciampa
title: Exclusive first look at Jamestown's Beech restaurant under new chef - NewsBreak
text:
By Gail Ciampa ,
19 hours ago Beech, the Jamestown restaurant that sits under a 130-year-old American Copper Beech tree, has a new chef and managing partner and a fresh menu.
James Beard Award -winning chef Michael Schlow, who won Best Chef Northeast for his Radius restaurant in Boston, will oversee Beech operations. His culinary team includes the return of Eric Warren as executive chef, who was in the kitchen when Beech opened in 2022 . For decades, the restaurant was Trattoria Simpatico and Simpatico.
The restaurant also had a makeover to repair the second-floor water damage from the February blizzard. The space has a new look and furnishings and can be used for small bridal parties and other private functions.
Beech's owners are the Conanicut Restaurant Group, which is comprised of longtime Jamestown residents. Many of them are friends of Schlow, he said in an exclusive interview with The Journal.
"I jumped at the chance. I've loved it as a guest," he said, adding that it has been his go-to spot when visiting the state.
"The investors have given us an opportunity here," he said. "We can make fun improvements without changing the ethos and DNA of the place."
Beech concept Schlow said he's excited to help develop the culture and the team that previous chef-partner Kevin Gadreau helped build.
He plans to evolve the concept to American meets Mediterranean.
"I create menus with chef Eric for what I want to eat," he said.
Chef Warren, a Jamestown native, has a far reach with community connections, Schlow said. That includes a relationship with Jamestown Community Farm , which has committed to growing everything from zucchini to specialty peppers just for their Beech kitchen.
"We want to be supportive of the local purveyors," he said. "We want to take advantage of fresh fish. Seafood and vegetables will be super local."
The Beech menu lineup includes meat, pasta and seafood, but Schlow said to expect a nightly list of specials. They will focus on the seasonal catch of the day, be it striped bass or local bay scallops.
Schlow's history A native of New York, Schlow's New England career began in Boston in 1995 with Cafe Louis. He opened Radius in 1999 and earned his James Beard award a year later.
Schlow is no stranger to Rhode Island. Back in 2022, he consulted on the brick oven pizza, sandwiches and other foods for Neon Marketplace , a very different gas station/convenience store concept. It was from the Procaccianti Companies that abandoned the concept when they leased it to Cumberland Farms in 2025.
That idea was close to his heart because on trips to Italy, his first stop is always at an Autogrill, a rest stop where one can get an espresso and panini. Neon was an opportunity to create that in the U.S., but it wasn't to be.
He has continued as a restaurateur, opening restaurants in Massachusetts, Michigan, Maryland and Washington, DC. He consulted on the former Seamark, a seafood restaurant and speakeasy at the Encore casino in Everett, Massachusetts. He is also a cookbook author.
What's on the menu at Beech?
Menu highlights include a Tuna Tartare with Cucumbers and Caviar; Spicy Ponzu Mussels Meuniere; Steak Frites with Bistro Sauce, Sauteed Spinach and Fries; Homemade Chitarra with Spicy Lobster; and Shrimp Diavola Chicken Milanese.
There will be a ceviche of the day as well as a Beech Chilled Seafood Plateau, which has an assortment of tartares, ceviches and shellfish appetizers.
As with most of his restaurants, he will have a signature Schlow Burger with fries on the menu, this one with Cheddar, crispy onions and a horseradish-black pepper sauce.
The Beech vibe Schlow understands the ebbs and flows of a seasonal restaurant from working in the Hamptons early in his career. "How you handle a summertime menu is completely different," he said.
Many diners will be people on vacation. Some will come over on a boat after a day on the water.
"We have to ask, 'What do people want from the restaurant?' " Schlow asked, then answered. "They want uncomplicated, well-seasoned, beautifully prepared food. They don’t want to be challenged," he said.
"I don’t want guests to have to look up ingredients on their phones," he added.
Schlow understands that a staff can get overwhelmed on busy nights. So he preaches his philosophy to think of each guest as an individual.
"Each person deserves to feel special," he said. "We know we can’t be perfect. But if we shoot for perfection, I think we can achieve excellence."
"Beech should be the place people want to come back to," he said. "Not cross it off a to-do list."
Details : Beech, 13 Narragansett Ave., Jamestown, 401-560-4051 beechjt.com . Sunday-Thursday 4:30-8:30 p.m.; Friday and Saturday: 4:30-9 p.m.
This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Exclusive first look at Jamestown's Beech restaurant under new chef
